# kimono

> AI Developer Lifecycle (DLC) wrapper for codebases — single or multi-repo — with a plug-and-play Claude skill catalog. The Rust binary handles workspace, git, and worktree operations; AI context generation and developer workflows (commit, PR, code review) live as installable Claude Code skills under `skills/`.

Kimono wraps repos into a workspace at `apps/<repo>/` (read-only clones, always on the default branch), uses git worktrees under `.worktrees/<repo>--<branch-slug>/` for active development, and exposes a `kimono plugins` CLI that installs skills from a registry (this same repo, by default). Installed skills land in the workspace's `.claude/skills/<name>/` and are recorded in `.kimono/config.yml > plugins.installed`. AI context (`CLAUDE.md`, per-project agent files, `.claude/settings.json`) is generated by the `bootstrap` and `discover` skills running inside Claude Code, not by the Rust binary.

## Core docs

- [README](README.md): public-facing overview, install, quick start
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): project-internal context, conventions, command reference
- [v2 spec](docs/specs/20260421-v2-spec.md): authoritative design — plugin system, skills, config schema, CLI surface
- [v2 implementation plan](docs/plans/20260514-v2-implementation-plan.md): how v2 was built, file structure, task decomposition

## Commands

CLI surface (`kimono <command>`):

- `init [name] [--from <path>] [--bare]`: interactive workspace setup; writes `.kimono/config.yml`, clones repos, installs the default skill bundle, optionally runs the bootstrap skill
- `add <name> <remote> [--branch <branch>]`: add a repo to the workspace
- `remove <name> [--delete]`: remove a repo (optionally delete files)
- `clone [repos...]`: clone all/some repos from config into `apps/`
- `sync [repos...] [--fetch-only]`: fetch + rebase repos to their default branch (skips dirty)
- `status [repos...]`: working tree state across repos — local only, no fetch
- `exec <command> [repos...]`: run a shell command in each repo
- `branch <name> [repos...] [--new] [--list] [--from-master] [--no-checkout]`: branch ops across repos (in `apps/`, not worktrees)
- `wt add <repo> <branch> [--new]`: create a worktree under `.worktrees/<repo>--<branch-slug>/`
- `wt remove <repo> <branch>`: remove a worktree
- `wt list [repo]`: list worktrees
- `wt feature <name> [repos...] [--new] [--remove]`: cross-repo feature worktrees in one command
- `wt clean [--merged] [--dry-run]`: clean up merged/stale worktrees
- `plugins list [--installed | --available]`: list catalog skills with install status
- `plugins search <query>`: search skills by name, description, or tag
- `plugins info <name>`: detailed info for one skill (includes local-vs-registry version)
- `plugins install [names...] [--version <x>]`: install skills (interactive MultiSelect picker when no names given)
- `plugins remove [names...]`: remove installed skills (interactive picker when no names given)
- `plugins update [names...]`: update installed skills against the registry
- `bootstrap`: launch interactive Claude Code session running the bootstrap skill
- `discover`: launch interactive Claude Code session running the discover skill
- `context show`: status of installed skills + presence of `CLAUDE.md` / agent files / settings

Alias: `kimono skills` is identical to `kimono plugins`.

## Skills

The skill catalog lives in this repo under `skills/`. Kimono shallow-clones the repo to `~/.cache/kimono/registry/` and installs skills into the workspace's `.claude/skills/<name>/`. Each skill is a single Markdown file with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) that Claude Code can invoke.

- [Skill catalog manifest](skills/index.json): all 7 default skills with name, description, version, tags, path
- [bootstrap skill](skills/bootstrap/SKILL.md): initial AI context setup — writes minimal `CLAUDE.md` and per-project agent files from config + manifests; light-touch, no source-tree walking
- [discover skill](skills/discover/SKILL.md): deep codebase scan — augments `CLAUDE.md` and agent files with architecture, domain vocabulary, hotspots; expensive, opt-in
- [git-commit skill](skills/git-commit/SKILL.md): stage and commit changes in worktrees with contextual messages; refuses to commit in `apps/`
- [create-pr skill](skills/create-pr/SKILL.md): push branch and open PR via `gh`; links cross-repo PRs in the same feature
- [update-pr skill](skills/update-pr/SKILL.md): push commits, refresh PR description, report check + review state
- [code-review skill](skills/code-review/SKILL.md): fetch PR review comments and structure them for the agent to address
- [hookify-rules skill](skills/hookify-rules/SKILL.md): generate `.claude/hookify/` rules enforcing the read-only master pattern; requires the hookify Claude Code plugin

## Config schema

`.kimono/config.yml` at workspace root:

```yaml
workspace:
  name: my-workspace
  apps_dir: apps              # default
  worktree_dir: .worktrees    # default
repos:
  backend:
    remote: git@github.com:org/backend.git
    branch: main              # default
    description: "NestJS GraphQL API"
    tech: [nestjs, typescript]
    package_manager: yarn
    depends_on: []
    commands:
      dev: yarn dev
plugins:
  registry: github.com/sand4rbh/kimono  # optional; defaults to the binary's baked-in URL
  installed:
    bootstrap: 1.0.0
```

Only `workspace.name` and at least one `repos.<name>.remote` are required.

## Workspace layout

```
my-workspace/                       # workspace root (a git repo)
├── .kimono/config.yml              # config + workspace marker
├── CLAUDE.md                       # written by the bootstrap skill
├── .claude/
│   ├── agents/<repo>.md            # one per project (multi-project: <repo>--<project>.md)
│   ├── settings.json
│   ├── skills/<name>/SKILL.md      # installed skills
│   └── hookify/                    # only if hookify-rules is installed
├── apps/<repo>/                    # read-only clone on default branch
└── .worktrees/<repo>--<slug>/      # active development
```
